passage: The client deck was due at five, and the printer had jammed, when Shreya leaned over Manjula's cubicle. "Have you heard? Ritesh's team is telling the director we're slow. We should tell her about their missed audit first." Manjula's phone buzzed. Two people in the pantry were already picking sides. She felt the pull to pass on a tale, just to be safe. "I'll pass on that," she said. "I'll say hi to Ritesh's team tomorrow like always. Can you check page six with me? The chart is wrong." Shreya shrugged, a little disappointed, but bent over the page. The deck went out at 4:58.

qa.q: What time did the deck go out?
qa.a: The deck went out at 4:58.

qa.q: What was Manjula tempted to do, and why?
qa.a: Manjula felt the pull to pass on a tale about the other team, just to be safe.

qa.q: How did Manjula stay friendly to everyone without taking sides?
qa.a: She declined to pass on the gossip, planned to greet Ritesh's team as usual, and turned Shreya's attention back to fixing the chart.

qa.q: How might Shreya see Manjula's refusal?
qa.a: Shreya seemed a little disappointed, perhaps expecting an ally, yet still helped with page six.

grounding: Gossip and groups pull a colleague in; she stays friendly to all, does good work and avoids taking sides.

passage:
Bhupen: Hi Alka, I'm Bhupen. I joined the accounts team on Monday. Where does everyone usually have lunch?
Alka: Oh! The terrace, around 1. Sorry, we just drift up there and never told you 🙂
Bhupen: No problem. I'll bring my tiffin. I kept thinking the team didn't like me 😅
Alka: Ha, no. We're just bad at inviting people. Give it a couple of weeks and you'll be sick of us.
Bhupen: Deal. Can I ask what the Friday chai group is?
Alka: Come on Friday. I'll save you a seat.

qa.q: Where does the team usually have lunch?
qa.a: They usually have lunch on the terrace, around 1.

qa.q: What was Bhupen worried about before messaging Alka?
qa.a: Bhupen worried that the team did not like Bhupen, because Bhupen had been left out of lunches.

qa.q: What small step did Bhupen take that helped?
qa.a: Bhupen said hello to Alka first, asked a simple question about lunch and asked about the Friday chai group. 🙂

qa.q: How does Alka see the situation?
qa.a: Alka thinks the team is just bad at inviting people, not hostile, so the leaving out was careless rather than unfriendly.

grounding: A newcomer left out of lunches says hello first and joins small conversations instead of assuming hostility.

passage: Vinita had spent three weeks scanning receipts and refilling the pantry at a small architecture studio, and her stipend barely covered her train fare. Rain hammered the windows the day she carried the fifth carton of files upstairs. She wanted to learn drafting. "Tejas sir, could I sit with the drawings team on Thursday? And could you tell me what I'm expected to learn here by the end of this month?" Tejas blinked, then admitted that the last intern never asked. "Try the site sketches. Show me on Friday." Vinita nodded and wrote it down. She decided that if she was still only carrying cartons at the end of the month, she would look for another internship.

qa.q: How many weeks had Vinita spent scanning receipts and refilling the pantry?
qa.a: She had spent three weeks doing it.

qa.q: What did Vinita want from the internship?
qa.a: Vinita wanted to learn drafting, not only carry cartons.

qa.q: What could Vinita do if the work does not change by the end of the month?
qa.a: Look for another internship, as she decided, since she asked for a clear role and feedback first.

qa.q: How might Tejas see Vinita's questions?
qa.a: Tejas blinked and admitted the last intern never asked, so the questions may have shown that the role had been left vague. 🙂

grounding: An intern given menial work with no learning asks for a clear role and feedback and decides when to move on.

passage: Sit, Rekha. You asked how to handle your first intern, so let me tell you about mine. I'm Simran, and when Aman joined, I was drowning in reconciliation sheets. I nearly handed all of them to him. Instead I sat with him for an hour and showed him one sheet from start to finish, and then I let him do the next while I watched. He found a formula error that I had missed for months. In the review I wrote it down by name: "Aman found and fixed the formula error." I could have let it pass as mine. Later he told me that was the day he decided to stay in finance. Teach slowly, Rekha. It pays back.

qa.q: How long did Simran sit with Aman on the first sheet?
qa.a: She sat with him for an hour.

qa.q: What did Simran nearly do when Aman joined, and what does that suggest she felt?
qa.a: She nearly handed all the sheets to him, which suggests she felt overwhelmed by the reconciliation work.

qa.q: What did Simran do that Rekha could copy with her own intern?
qa.a: Show one task from start to finish, let the intern try the next while watching, and credit the intern's finds by name. 🙂

qa.q: How did Aman feel after being named in the review?
qa.a: Aman decided that day to stay in finance, which suggests he felt valued and respected.

grounding: A colleague now teaches an intern patiently and credits the contribution instead of dumping tasks.

passage: HR note, Wednesday. Sharmila, a junior designer, met me privately. She said a senior colleague from another floor has commented on her clothes and repeatedly asked her out, even after she said no in clear words twice. She had kept a dated list of the messages and the days it happened. She kept asking whether she was overreacting. I told her plainly that it is not her fault and that saying no was enough. I explained that the POSH committee handles such complaints and that she can file a written one; I gave her the form and the committee member's contact details. I did not ask her to confront the colleague herself. She said she would think about it until Friday. I will check in with her then. Minakshi, HR officer

qa.q: Where does the senior colleague work?
qa.a: The senior colleague works on another floor.

qa.q: Why did Sharmila keep asking whether she was overreacting?
qa.a: She seems unsure whether her reaction is justified and may fear she is at fault, which the HR officer answered by saying it is not her fault.

qa.q: What steps helped Sharmila in this meeting?
qa.a: She had kept a dated list of messages, learned how the POSH committee works, and received the form and contact details without being pushed to confront the colleague.

qa.q: What might it mean for Sharmila that Minakshi will check in on Friday?
qa.a: It means Sharmila is not left alone with the decision and can come back with questions.

grounding: A junior faces unwelcome comments and advances; the response is saying no, documenting dates and using the POSH committee.

passage: At Monday's meeting in the Johannesburg office, Lucia showed a slide titled "Route Consolidation Plan" and said, "I've been working on this." Thabo recognised every line. He had emailed her the same numbers last Wednesday. His face grew hot as their manager, Ms Dlamini, nodded approvingly. He did not speak. Afterwards he found Lucia at the kettle. "Lucia, that plan came from the sheet I sent you on the fourteenth. Can we tell Ms Dlamini it was joint work?" Lucia hesitated, then said she had forgotten to mention it. That evening Thabo saved his sent email with its date and wrote Lucia a short recap of who had done which part. From then on he sent his updates to the whole team.

qa.q: What was the title of Lucia's slide?
qa.a: The slide was titled "Route Consolidation Plan."

qa.q: How did Thabo feel when Lucia presented his numbers, and how can you tell?
qa.a: He felt hurt and angry, shown by his face growing hot, yet he stayed silent in the meeting.

qa.q: What did Thabo do that prevents this happening again?
qa.a: He raised it calmly with Lucia in private, kept the dated email, sent a recap of roles, and began sending updates to the whole team.

qa.q: How might Lucia see the conversation at the kettle?
qa.a: Lucia hesitated and said she had forgotten, which may mean she was caught off guard or embarrassed rather than openly defensive. 😅

grounding: A colleague presents Thabo's work as her own; he raises it calmly with evidence and shares updates in writing.

passage: The lift doors were closing when the director asked, "Who came up with the churn analysis?" Nikita opened her mouth. Tanuja had built the model over two weekends, and Nikita had only made the slides. For a second the word "I" sat ready on her tongue, because promotion talks were next month. "Tanuja built the model. I turned it into slides," she said instead, holding the door. The director looked at them both. "Good. Put both names on the summary." Nikita's heart was pounding, half regret and half relief. In the lift she told herself it had cost her nothing yet, and knew that was not quite true.

qa.q: Who built the churn analysis model?
qa.a: Tanuja built the model over two weekends.

qa.q: What was Nikita tempted to do, and what was on her mind?
qa.a: She was tempted to say "I" and take the credit, because promotion talks were next month.

qa.q: Why does naming who did what matter for the team later?
qa.a: It builds trust, and the director asked for both names on the summary, so both people are recognised. 🙂

qa.q: How might Tanuja have felt hearing Nikita's answer?
qa.a: Tanuja probably felt relieved and valued, since the real work was named instead of being passed off.

grounding: A colleague is tempted to present shared work as her own but names who did what.

passage: Tanvir's diary, Tuesday night. Damini told our manager today that the wrong figures in the sales report were mine. In front of everyone. My face went hot and I wanted to snap back, "You entered those numbers!" I didn't. I said, "I can check." At my desk I opened the file history. The change was made on Monday from her login. I printed it. I am not going to accuse her tomorrow. I will show the manager the record and ask how we fix the report. Part of me still wants revenge, and I am going to sleep on that instead of acting. 😔 Tanvir

qa.q: When was the change made to the sales report?
qa.a: The change was made on Monday from Damini's login.

qa.q: What did Tanvir feel and want when Damini blamed him?
qa.a: He felt his face go hot and wanted to snap back, but he held it in and offered to check.

qa.q: What is Tanvir's plan for tomorrow, and why is it a good one?
qa.a: He will show the manager the printed record and ask how to fix the report, which relies on facts rather than accusing or retaliating.

qa.q: How might Damini see the moment when the record is shown?
qa.a: Damini may feel exposed or defensive, which is why Tanvir plans to focus on fixing the report instead of blaming.

grounding: A colleague blames Tanvir for a mistake; he stays calm, presents facts and involves the manager.

passage: Sunday night. Group project due Friday and I have written the whole report again. Shreya said "I'll do slides" and sent nothing. The other two just react with thumbs-up. I felt so resentful that I nearly typed a long message in the group chat. Instead I decided to be practical. Tomorrow I will post a list with each person's part and a day, and ask everyone to update by Wednesday. If I had set roles at the start, that was my miss too. If nothing moves, I will tell our teacher before the deadline, not after. I am tired but calmer. 🙂 Manjula

qa.q: What did Shreya say she would do?
qa.a: Shreya said she would do the slides.

qa.q: What did Manjula feel and want to do when nobody helped?
qa.a: She felt so resentful that she nearly typed a long message in the group chat, but chose a practical plan instead.

qa.q: What could Manjula do if the group still does not move?
qa.a: Tell the teacher before the deadline, not after, as she plans, after posting the list of parts and days.

qa.q: How might Shreya see Manjula's list of parts and days?
qa.a: Shreya may see it as a clear, fair request, or feel a little caught out about the slides, but it gives a way to start.

grounding: A groupmate carries the load while others do little and sets roles and check-ins and raises it before the deadline.

passage: I'm Samir. In our marketing group project I did almost nothing for two weeks, because Francis always finished things early and I told myself he would cover it. Then, the night before the presentation, I walked into the library and saw Francis with red eyes and three empty tea cups, still fixing my survey section. I felt a sharp pang, half guilt and half shame. I sat down and did the charts I owed. At the presentation the teacher asked who had done the analysis. "Francis did the analysis. I did the charts," I said. It was true, and it was smaller than I had wanted it to be. I'm not proud of the two weeks before it.

qa.q: How many empty tea cups were by Francis in the library?
qa.a: There were three empty tea cups.

qa.q: What did Samir feel when he saw Francis fixing the survey section?
qa.a: Samir felt a sharp pang, half guilt and half shame, at seeing how much Francis was carrying.

qa.q: What did Samir do to put the unfairness right?
qa.a: He sat down and did the charts he owed, and at the presentation he named who did what without claiming more.

qa.q: How might Francis have felt covering the survey section?
qa.a: Francis was tired, with red eyes, and may have felt unfairly loaded even without saying so.

grounding: A groupmate slacks off because others will cover, sees the unfairness, contributes and does not claim extra credit.
